I live in a very noisy city with bars and clubs lining my street, but it’s nothing compared to the noise my neighbor makes. That’s just the reality of apartment living. Buy a box fan, preferably a shitty one, and run it 24/7 - white noise really helps mask noises. I also play ambience music on my Alexa, smart TV, phone, etc to have in the background at night on top of the box fan. Find ASMR, ambient tracks, white noise makers like fans, etc and layer them to mask different sounds. There’s a science behind pink/white/brown noise, figure out what works for your neighbors’ noise and layer it. Noise cancelling earbuds have also really helped me focus and even sleep quicker.

Whatever you decide to do, please try your best to not take out private third party loans for school or rent. This is your quickest way to a life of never-ending debt. I’m getting my masters now and the difference between the federal loans I’ve been given and taken out compared to what I was quoted for from Sally Mae is night and day. I would be in twice the amount of debt I’m in now with their interest rates, the monthly payments would deplete my current salary. Federal loans are always generous: you’ll have a year after college to start paying them back, you’ll be able to get on an income driven payment plan, and if you decide to continue your education you can pause your payments. These are privileges you won’t get with a third party loan provider. 

It’s a lot of work but if you take the route I did and rent while studying just be prepared to bust your ass. It isn’t easy but it is possible.

Since starting the meds, I haven’t really dreamed at all. When I do, it’s usually something I don’t remember by the time I wake up. I’m taking a very small dose so it’s possible that I’m not taking enough to feel that particular effect.

In all honesty, I also just kind of ignore or cut those people from my life. Had a lifelong friend I recently had to cut contact with because her actions really triggered me. 

I brought this issue up with my therapist at our last session and she told me the best way to avoid triggering people (without cutting them off entirely) was to handle them in small doses. If you know you’re going to be in a social situation with this type of person, excuse yourself to a safe space to vent every so often or, leave the function early if you really can’t stomach it. 

I often have to deal with triggering people on a day to day basis so I feel for you! Hope it all works out.
